name: Todd Young
stance: Pro-innovation but safety-engaged: presses the government to track frontier-model risks — interpretability, incident and vulnerability reporting, federal test-and-evaluation, and critical-infrastructure safeguards.

statements.text: Co-introduced the bipartisan Future of AI Innovation Act with Sens. Hickenlooper, Cantwell, and Blackburn, authorizing the NIST AI Safety Institute to develop AI standards and creating public-private testbeds to evaluate models.
There, there's some threats out there that are being discussed. I mean, if AI technologies enable one to more effectively, more easily develop superbugs,
Imagine a world in which those things don’t happen because we don’t appreciate the opportunity cost of over regulating,
Welcomed the White House national AI legislative framework and said he looks forward to partnering on its goals.
This is a positive development. Similar lines of communication existed during the Cold War and helped lower the chance of dangerous misperceptions.

Wrote to the National Security Advisor urging the NSC to convene recurring roundtables with frontier-AI developers and national-security experts, and to pursue voluntary AI incident and vulnerability reporting, interpretability research, federal test-and-evaluation environments, and safeguards against AI-enabled attacks on critical infrastructure.

Recent developments involving frontier AI models have further demonstrated the ability of advanced systems to circumvent safeguards, interact with external systems, and substantially enhance offensive cyber capabilities.
We must also continue to improve our understanding of these increasingly complex systems, whose internal processes can be difficult even for experts to fully interpret, predict, and control
I am calling for the National Security Council to hold regular meetings on the emerging national security threats posed by advanced AI systems.
